items.title: Lovie Austin Interview, 1969-04-25
items.q: There's a man down in New Orleans now, Dave Oxley, that was in that show, told me all about it.

ctx.x: They used to come there with a carnival, and it happened in a vacant lot. And Bessie and I used to sit out in the back of the carnival because we couldn't go in. Yeah. We'd sit out there, and Maureen would sing, Oh, these dogs of mine, that's a little torture. Yeah, I remember that. And we would sit back out there, and she would imitate Maureen singing. She would learn. That's the way she learned how to sing. And she was here with me just before she went away. See, she went down to Memphis, and her brother was…

Yes, sir. There's a man down in New Orleans now, Dave Oxley, that was in that show, told me all about it. Mm-hmm. Did you ever know Clarence Williams in New York? I guess you would have, but I knew him. I knew Clarence Williams here. Oh, when he was last right, he had the music store here.
Right down there on State Street.
